message.content:
**Answer:**  
One of the most celebrated sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser)** by French artist **Auguste Rodin** (1889).

**Why it’s so famous**

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Date** | 1889 (first cast) |
| **Medium** | Bronze (originally a plaster study) |
| **Style** | Realist/Impressionist blend – a tender, almost sensual embrace between two figures |
| **Influence** | It became a symbol of romantic love and a benchmark for modern sculpture; its expressive form broke away from the rigid academic style of the time. |
| **Locations** | Casts exist worldwide – Musée Rodin (Paris), National Gallery of Art (Washington, D.C.), Museum of Fine Arts (Boston), and many others. |
| **Legacy** | Frequently reproduced, referenced in literature, film, and popular culture; it helped cement Rodin’s reputation as a pioneer of modern sculpture. |

**Contextual note**  
While Rodin’s “The Thinker” (1902‑03) is often cited as his masterpiece, it belongs to the early 20th century. “The Kiss,” completed in 1889, sits squarely in the late 19th century and remains one of the era’s most iconic works.
